title: Every sentence mark sits in a pause
statement: Check that every sentence mark in a read-along narration clip sits in a pause, because a mark inside speech cuts off the previous line's last word.
detail: The reading course renderer's closing-questions handover gives every narration clip one mark per sentence and says to verify each new clip in two ways: read it back with speech-to-text word for word, and check that every mark sits in a pause, since a mark inside speech cuts the previous line's last word (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/handover/closing-questions/HANDOVER.md`, lines 252-264). The same handover prefers splicing a changed sentence into the original take, cut at pauses measured by silence detection, to re-recording the line.

evidence.quote: **Verify every clip**: read it back with Gemini speech-to-text word for word, and check every mark sits in a pause (a mark inside speech cuts the previous line's last word).
there is one mark per sentence
when a line changes by a sentence, keep the original take and synthesise only the new sentence, cutting at measured pauses
